thread:
renee: trying out the java sampleapp + go-sdk parity test. batcher sends 5 inputs, backend returns 5 embeddings but item 4 has 0-length embedding array.
tobias: 0-length? that's wild. what model and SDK versions?
renee: model openembed-1536, java-sample 0.5.0, go-sdk v0.8.0. curl to API returns valid vectors. this only shows up via our combined sampleapp + local proxy.
lucy: any chance of JSON parsing bug or streaming chunk cutoff?
renee: dug in. stack traces show the client retry path for 429 does a partial re-encode and then merges responses from first and replay. if the server returns a 204 for a small item (edge-case) the merge logic ignores that item. minimal repro attached below.
tobias: paste repro?
renee: gist-like snippet: \n```java\n// batch helper pseudo\nList<byte[]> frames = concat(inputs);
send(frames);
// on retry, we merge oldResponses + newResponses by index
for (i=0;i<n;i++) {
  merged[i] = oldResponses[i] != null ? oldResponses[i] : newResponses[j++];
}
```
renee: flaw is the index mapping when oldResponses has sparse nulls. we end up with null/empty embedding slot which gets serialized as [] to client.
lucy: that explains 0-length. fix: normalize arrays and use request-id mapping rather than naive index merging.
tobias: also, we should validate response shapes server-side and reject mismatches with 422 instead of letting client continue. saves customers from silent downstream failures.
infra-bot: created ticket INF-2401: "batch-merge-sparse-null-fix + server-side-dim-validation". linked to pipeline #901.
renee: good. alternative mitigation: client should check returned embedding length equals model.dim and raise error. avoid returning partially merged results.
lucy: agree. i'll add a unit test for sparse-response merge behavior across java/go/node sdks to ensure parity.
tobias: another gotcha: our rerank helper pairs embeddings by position; if an embedding is missing we silently shift others and return incorrect scores. require embedding ID or request-id in pairing to avoid position-based coupling.
renee: filed a small docs PR to add a note about recommending x-rdw-request-id for all batch calls to guarantee idempotency and pairing stability.
qa-bot: added regression test case to nightly e2e suite: embed-batch-retry-merge.
renee: thanks all. this was causing confusion for new users trying the sampleapp; will follow up with a patch to java-sample and the go-sdk. :raised_hands:
